mechanism: Two differently colored original quarter-arcs pair the actual black-side and white-side printed features to D, following only the upward flip and neglecting the preceding leftward flip. The candidate retains all fills, arrow paths, blank-back cards and option orientations.
mathematical_solution: Use local coordinates about the card centre with x right and y up. A left flip reflects (x,y) to (-x,y), exposing the plain back; the subsequent upward flip reflects the card coordinates to (-x,-y) and returns the printed side. The original printed semicircle occupies y<0 with black quarter x<0,y<0. The final printed semicircle therefore occupies y>0 with its black quarter x>0,y>0. Only A has upper semicircle and black right quarter. D has black left quarter and is the result of just the upward reflection. B and E have vertical semicircles, and C remains below. Original black fill and its white counterpart remain visibly unchanged; colored original outer arcs impose no new physical ink-continuity requirement.
human_semantics: Four partial style changes only, on existing outer arcs. They do not create cuts or regions. Black/white areas, the central radius, diameter, both original flip arrows, question mark and all option letters remain clear. The false correspondence can be rejected by the first horizontal reflection.

marker_roles.role: The input lower-left quarter-arc adjacent to the original black region; first concrete feature to track.
The input lower-right quarter-arc adjacent to the white region; complementary feature, preserving the visible black/white division.
D upper-left quarter-arc falsely paired with the input black-side quarter: a single upward flip preserves left/right, but the prior left flip must reverse it.
D upper-right white-side quarter paired with the source white-side quarter; completes the false single-flip correspondence rather than an isolated option highlight.
